label: Bonus Class 1
title: How English Sounds Work: Lazy A, Quick E and Smiley I
titleAr: كيف تعمل أصوات الإنجليزية: A الكسولة و E السريعة و I المبتسمة
bigIdea: Letters are what we see; sounds are what we hear. English has only 5 vowel letters but many more vowel sounds, so we must train our mouth and our ears.
bigIdeaAr: الحروف هي ما نراه، والأصوات هي ما نسمعه. في الإنجليزية 5 حروف متحركة فقط لكن أصواتها أكثر بكثير، لذلك ندرّب الفم والأذن معاً.
builtOn: Lessons 1-4: This is... / I am... / It is a... / big and small
Phonics groups 1-2 (Lessons 1 and 3): s, a, t, p, i, n, m, d

objectives.en: I can say the difference between a letter and a sound.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أفرّق بين الحرف والصوت.

objectives.en: I can tell a consonant sound from a vowel sound.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أميّز الصوت الساكن من الصوت المتحرك.

objectives.en: I can hear and say the short vowels a (cat), e (bed) and i (sit).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أسمع وأنطق الأصوات القصيرة a و e و i.

objectives.en: I can change one vowel to make a new word (pan, pen, pin).
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أغيّر صوتاً واحداً لأصنع كلمة جديدة.

keyTerms.meaning: What you hear when someone speaks.
An open-mouth sound: the air flows out freely. Vowel letters: a, e, i, o, u.
A sound where the lips, teeth or tongue stop or squeeze the air.
Two words that are the same except for one sound: pen / pin.

linguisticsCorner.title: Your mouth is a sound machine

facts.en: Every sound is made by moving air. The lips, teeth and tongue shape the air, like hands shaping clay.
facts.ar: كل صوت يصنعه الهواء المتحرك. الشفتان والأسنان واللسان تشكّل الهواء كما تشكّل اليدان الصلصال.

facts.en: Consonants: something blocks or squeezes the air (m = lips close, s = teeth hiss, t = tongue taps).
facts.ar: الأصوات الساكنة: شيء ما يوقف الهواء أو يضغطه (m الشفتان تُغلقان، s صفير بين الأسنان، t نقرة اللسان).

facts.en: Vowels: the mouth stays open and the air flows. The jaw moves like an elevator: wide open for a, middle for e, almost closed for i.
facts.ar: الأصوات المتحركة: الفم يبقى مفتوحاً والهواء يمرّ. الفك يتحرك كالمصعد: مفتوح جداً مع a، في الوسط مع e، شبه مغلق مع i.

facts.en: English has 5 vowel letters but about 12 vowel sounds (plus sliding sounds like 'ay' and 'oy'). That is why the same letter can sound different.
facts.ar: في الإنجليزية 5 حروف متحركة لكن نحو 12 صوتاً متحركاً (إضافة إلى أصوات منزلقة مثل ay و oy)، ولهذا قد يُنطق الحرف نفسه بطرق مختلفة.

arabicBridge.point: Close to Arabic fatha, but Lazy A opens the mouth wider and takes a little longer.
arabicBridge.pointAr: قريبة من الفتحة، لكن A الكسولة تفتح الفم أكثر وتأخذ وقتاً أطول قليلاً.

arabicBridge.point: Arabic has no separate letter or mark for this sound. It sits between fatha and kasra: short and quick.
arabicBridge.pointAr: لا توجد له علامة خاصة في العربية؛ هو بين الفتحة والكسرة: قصير وسريع.

arabicBridge.point: Close to Arabic kasra. Keep it short and relaxed; do not stretch it into 'ee' (seat).
arabicBridge.pointAr: قريب من الكسرة. اجعله قصيراً ومرتاحاً، ولا تمدّه إلى ee كما في seat.

arabicBridge.arabic: 3 حركات قصيرة (فتحة، كسرة، ضمة) + 3 حروف مدّ (ا، و، ي)
arabicBridge.point: Arabic shows short vowels with small marks above and below letters; English always writes the vowel as a full letter inside the word.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تُظهر الحركات القصيرة بعلامات صغيرة فوق الحروف وتحتها، أما الإنجليزية فتكتب الصوت المتحرك حرفاً كاملاً داخل الكلمة.

commonErrors.why: Arabic has no separate e sound, so e often slides up to i. Use the Vowel Elevator: e is the middle floor.
Fatha covers both a and e for Arabic ears. Quick E is shorter and the mouth is less open.
Stretching i into the long ee sound. Smiley I is tiny and quick.

teacher: Three vowel character cards: Lazy A (yawning), Quick E (running), Smiley I (tiny smile)
Word cards: pan, pen, pin, bag, beg, big, sat, set, sit, tan, ten, tin
A small hand mirror or the webcam self-view
student: A small mirror (or the camera self-view)
Three paper cards with big letters: a, e, i

stages.name: Warm-up: Sound Hunt
stages.method: Listening hook with closed eyes (attention and curiosity)
stages.purpose: Switch on the ears and show that sounds carry meaning before we ever see a letter.
teacherSays: Hello, Sound Scientists! Close your eyes. Listen... What is it?
(Clap.) A clap! (Hiss sss.) A snake! (Say mmm.) Yummy food!
Today your mouth is a music machine. Let's find out how it works!
teacherSaysAr: أغمضوا عيونكم واسمعوا... ما هذا الصوت؟
اليوم فمكم آلة موسيقية، هيا نكتشف كيف تعمل!
studentsDo: Close eyes and guess 4 sounds (clap, sss, mmm, a knock).
Copy each mouth sound: sss, mmm, t-t-t.
tips: Keep it fast and playful; the goal is attention, not accuracy.
Make the last two sounds speech sounds (sss, mmm) to lead into the next stage.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: Letters vs Sounds and the Sound Machine
stages.nameAr: ركن اللغويات: الحروف والأصوات وآلة الصوت
stages.method: Guided discovery with mirrors and touch (multisensory phonics)
stages.purpose: Learn that letters are seen and sounds are heard, and that consonants block the air while vowels let it flow.
teacherSays: This is the letter S. Its name is 'ess'. But its sound is sss. Name: ess. Sound: sss.
Take your mirror. Say mmm. What do your lips do? They close! M is a lips sound.
Now sss. Your teeth are together and the air hisses. Now t-t-t: your tongue taps behind your teeth.
These are consonants: something stops or squeezes the air.
Now say aaa. Open! The air flows out. Nothing stops it. This is a vowel.
Put your hand on your throat. Say zzz... buzz! Now sss... no buzz. Some sounds buzz, some whisper.
teacherSaysAr: اسم الحرف شيء، وصوته شيء آخر.
الصوت الساكن: شيء يوقف الهواء. الصوت المتحرك: الفم مفتوح والهواء يمرّ.
studentsDo: Say the name and the sound of s, t, m, p, a.
Use the mirror to watch lips, teeth and tongue for m, s, t, p.
Hand on throat: feel buzz (z, m, n) and no buzz (s, t, p).
Sort sounds into two boxes on the slide: Stop sounds (consonants) and Open sounds (vowels).

exercise.instructions: Say the sound. Is the air blocked or free? Put it in the right box.
exercise.instructionsAr: انطق الصوت. هل الهواء محبوس أم حر؟ ضعه في الصندوق الصحيح.

tips: Say sounds pure and short: 'm' not 'muh', 't' not 'tuh'.
Children who have no mirror can use the camera self-view.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: Fatha, Kasra and the English Vowels
stages.nameAr: جسر العربية: الفتحة والكسرة وأصوات الإنجليزية
stages.method: Contrastive analysis: use what children already know in Arabic
stages.purpose: Connect English short vowels to Arabic harakat and show why e is the new, tricky one.
teacherSays: In Arabic we say بَ بِ بُ: ba, bi, bu. Three short vowels: fatha, kasra, damma.
English has five vowel letters: a, e, i, o, u. And many more vowel sounds!
Fatha is close to a in cat. Kasra is close to i in sit.
But English has a new sound between them: e in bed. Arabic has no mark for it. It is our new friend!
In Arabic we often do not write short vowels. In English, the vowel is always written inside the word: c-a-t.
teacherSaysAr: الفتحة قريبة من a، والكسرة قريبة من i، أما e فصوت جديد بينهما.
في الإنجليزية نكتب الحركة حرفاً داخل الكلمة دائماً.
studentsDo: Read بَ بِ بُ aloud, then say bag, big.
Point to where e sits between fatha and kasra on the slide's 'vowel bridge'.
Spot the vowel letter in cat, bed, sit (write it in the chat or show the card).
tips: Keep the comparison simple: 'close to', not 'the same as'.
Celebrate that Arabic speakers already own two of the three sounds.

stages.name: Meet the Vowel Friends: Lazy A, Quick E, Smiley I
stages.nameAr: تعرّف على أصدقاء الحركات: A الكسولة و E السريعة و I المبتسمة
stages.method: Character mnemonics + gesture (TPR) + the Vowel Elevator (jaw height)
stages.purpose: Give each short vowel a memorable character, a gesture and a mouth position.
teacherSays: This is Lazy A. She is sleepy. She opens her mouth WIDE and takes her time: aaa... cat, bag, pan. (Yawn gesture: hands open wide.)
This is Quick E. He is always in a hurry! Short and fast: e! bed, pen, ten. (Quick finger point.)
This is Smiley I. She is tiny and smiles a little: i! sit, big, pin. (Small pinch with two fingers.)
Now the Vowel Elevator! Your jaw is the elevator. Ground floor, mouth wide: a. Middle floor: e. Top floor, almost closed: i. Up we go: a... e... i!
Watch my mouth, then watch yours in the mirror.
teacherSaysAr: A كسولة: تفتح فمها كثيراً وتتمهل. E مستعجلة دائماً: قصيرة وسريعة. I صغيرة ومبتسمة.
الفك مثل المصعد: الطابق الأرضي a، الأوسط e، الأعلى i.
studentsDo: Copy each character's sound and gesture three times.
Ride the Vowel Elevator with hand on chin: a-e-i, i-e-a.
Echo the word trios after the teacher: pan, pen, pin / bag, beg, big / sat, set, sit / tan, ten, tin.

exercise.instructions: Listen, watch the mouth, then say it back with the gesture.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع وراقب الفم ثم كرر مع الحركة.

tips: Exaggerate the jaw movement at first, then make it natural.
Lazy A really is a little longer than E and I in natural English, so the story matches the phonetics.

stages.name: Ear Training: Show Me the Friend!
stages.method: Minimal-pair listening with whole-class response (TPR cards)
stages.purpose: Train the ear to hear a, e and i apart, then check every child quickly.
teacherSays: I say a word. You show me the friend: Lazy A, Quick E or Smiley I. Ready?
Hold up your card... 3, 2, 1, show me!
Odd one out! Listen: mat, sat, sit. Which one is different?
teacherSaysAr: أقول كلمة، وأنت ترفع بطاقة الصديق الصحيح.
studentsDo: Hold up the a, e or i card (or do the gesture) for each word.
Find the odd one out in 4 sets.
Take turns being the teacher: say a word for the group to show.

exercise.instructions: Listen to the word. Show the right vowel card.
exercise.instructionsAr: استمع للكلمة وارفع بطاقة الحرف الصحيح.

items.prompt: odd one out: mat, sat, sit
odd one out: pen, ten, pan
odd one out: pin, tin, ten
odd one out: bed, red, bad

tips: Say the word naturally the first time and slowly the second time.
Watch for children who copy their friends; ask them to close eyes and then show.

stages.name: Mouth Gym: Swap the Vowel and Tongue Twisters
stages.nameAr: رياضة الفم: بدّل الحركة وجمل صعبة النطق
stages.method: Phoneme substitution (word building) + choral and solo production
stages.purpose: Move from hearing to saying and spelling: change one vowel to make a new word.
teacherSays: Magic swap! p-a-n is pan. Swap a for e... p-e-n: pen! Swap e for i... pin!
Your turn: b-a-g. Swap a for i. What is it?
Now our tongue twisters. Slowly first, then fast!
teacherSaysAr: بدّل الحرف المتحرك فقط لتصنع كلمة جديدة.
studentsDo: Build words on paper by swapping the middle letter: p_n, b_g, s_t, t_n.
Read the new word aloud and do the friend's gesture.
Say the three twisters: 'Lazy A sat on a mat.' / 'Quick E met ten men.' / 'Smiley I sits in a big pit.'
Speed round: each child says one twister alone; the group claps when the vowels are clear.

exercise.instructions: Change the vowel to make a new word. Write it and say it.
exercise.instructionsAr: غيّر الحرف المتحرك لتصنع كلمة جديدة، اكتبها وانطقها.

tips: If a child says pin for pen, use the elevator: 'One floor down!'

stages.name: Exit Ticket, Did You Know? and Goodbye
stages.purpose: See which children can hear a, e and i alone, and finish with a fact to share at home.
teacherSays: Exit ticket! I say five words. Write only the vowel letter: a, e or i.
Did you know? English has only 5 vowel letters but about 12 vowel sounds. Arabic has 3 short vowels and 3 long ones. You are learning a new sound system - that is real science!
Your mission at home: teach your family Lazy A, Quick E and Smiley I!
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ في الإنجليزية 5 حروف متحركة لكن نحو 12 صوتاً متحركاً!
مهمتك في البيت: علّم عائلتك الأصدقاء الثلاثة!
studentsDo: Write the vowel for 5 words.
Say goodbye using a vowel friend: 'Bye-bye, Quick E!'
tips: Note who scored under 4/5 for extra practice in Lessons 5-7 warm-ups.

exitTicket.instructions: Listen. Write the vowel letter you hear: a, e or i.
exitTicket.instructionsAr: استمع واكتب الحرف المتحرك الذي تسمعه: a أو e أو i.

homework.en: Mirror Mission: say pan, pen, pin to someone at home and show the elevator. Then find 3 things at home with a, e or i in the middle (bag, bed, sink...) and say them.
homework.ar: مهمة المرآة: قل pan و pen و pin لأحد أفراد أسرتك وأرِه المصعد. ثم ابحث عن 3 أشياء في البيت فيها a أو e أو i في الوسط وانطقها.
tasks: Say the three tongue twisters to a family member.
Draw Lazy A, Quick E and Smiley I and write one word under each.
Find 3 objects at home and sort them by vowel.

support: Use only two vowels (a and i) first, then add e.
Let the child do the gesture instead of writing the letter.
Give the word with a picture for every listening item.
challenge: Add o and u with a five-word family: hat, het (not a word!), hit, hot, hut. Which ones are real words?
Make a 4-word chain by changing one sound at a time: pan, pen, ten, tin.
Invent a new tongue twister with Quick E.

successCriteria: Explains in their own words (English or Arabic) the difference between a letter and a sound.
Sorts at least 6 of 8 sounds correctly as consonant or vowel.
Shows the right vowel card for at least 8 of 12 listening items.
Says pan / pen / pin with three clearly different vowels.

teacherNotes: This class is about the system, not new vocabulary: almost every word is a short CVC word the children can already decode.
Keep English instructions short and repeat them in Arabic only when needed.
Reuse the three characters and the elevator gesture in later warm-ups: they are the class's shared language for vowels.
Bonus Class 2 builds on this with the sounds Arabic does not have (p, v) and the short o and u.
